Cusco · Perú

Tambomachay

Water moving through Inca masonry

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

Water emerges through fitted masonry and drops between levels. The sound changes as you approach the fountains, making it easier to distinguish the working water system from the terraces behind it. The popular name “Inca baths” describes an interpretation of the waterworks.

Planning your visit

30–45 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

Water moving through Inca masonry

Use the viewpoint across from the outlets so that the falling water is outlined against darker masonry. A close-up alone can hide the difference in height between the channels.

History and local experience

Look for the junctions hidden within the retaining walls. Water seems to appear instantly at each outlet precisely because much of its journey is concealed inside the masonry.

Walking route

  1. Tambomachay, carretera Cusco–Pisac
  2. Walk from the control post toward the sound of the springs, stop on the visitor side opposite the outlets and follow the descending channels with your eyes.
  3. Photograph from the path without entering the watercourse.
